checks.title: OneDrive signs people in and moves their folders without asking
remediation: In an Intune settings catalog profile for Windows, enable Silently sign in users to the OneDrive sync app with their Windows credentials.
In the same profile, enable Silently move Windows known folders to OneDrive with the tenant ID, and Prevent users from moving their Windows known folders back.
Assign it to a pilot group, then to all Windows devices, staying under 1,000 devices a day while folders upload.

userImpact.text: People find OneDrive already signed in and their Desktop, Documents and Pictures backed up, with a notification the first time.

checks.narrative: Without these settings people must sign in to OneDrive themselves and choose to back up their folders, and many never do. With them, a new or replaced PC has the person's files in a few minutes and a lost laptop costs nothing but the hardware.

checks.title: Edge browser sign-in not turned off
remediation: Open each policy listed and remove the Browser sign-in settings value Disable browser sign-in, or set it to Allow users to sign-in.
If profiles must stay separate, keep sign-in allowed and control sync with the sync policies instead.

userImpact.text: Edge opens signed in with the work account, so favourites and passwords follow people between devices and work sites sign in on their own.

checks.narrative: Turning browser sign-in off, often copied from a hardening guide, means Edge never picks up the work account. People then sign in to every site by hand and lose single sign-on to Microsoft 365 in the browser, with no security gain on a managed device.

checks.title: New Windows devices show setup progress
remediation: In Intune, Devices, Enrollment, Windows, Enrollment Status Page, edit the default profile or create one for your Autopilot devices.
Set Show app and profile configuration progress to Yes, choose the apps that must install before the desktop, and allow the user to reset the device if installation fails.
Assign it to all devices or the Autopilot group.

userImpact.text: People see their apps and settings arriving during setup instead of reaching a half-ready desktop.

checks.narrative: Without the Enrollment Status Page a new device reaches the desktop before its apps and policies arrive, and the first hour is spent wondering where Outlook is. With it, setup waits until the essentials are installed and tells the person what is happening.

checks.title: Windows settings backup and restore turned on
remediation: In Intune, Devices, Enrollment, Windows, turn on Show restore page for Windows settings backup and restore (verify the label).
Allow Windows backup on devices through the settings catalog so there is something to restore.
Use user-driven Autopilot; restore does not run in self-deploying mode or on hybrid joined devices.

userImpact.text: On a new device people are offered their wallpaper, settings and pinned apps from the old one.

checks.narrative: Windows settings backup and restore brings a person's settings and pinned apps to a replacement device during setup. It is off until an administrator turns it on, and it makes a device swap feel like the same machine.

checks.title: Autopilot names new devices consistently
remediation: Edit each Autopilot profile listed and set Apply device name template, for example a prefix and %SERIAL%.
Check the template fits in 15 characters, the limit Windows allows.

userImpact.text: Devices get names the help desk can read; people notice nothing.

checks.narrative: Without a template, Autopilot devices are named DESKTOP- and a random string, and nobody can tell from the name whose device it is or where it belongs. A template makes support calls, reports and Conditional Access logs readable.

checks.title: The sign-in page carries the organisation's logo and words
remediation: In Entra, Company branding, edit the default sign-in experience.
Add the banner logo and square logo, and a short sign-in page text people will recognise.
Keep the default background unless brand guidelines say otherwise.

userImpact.text: People see a familiar page when they sign in, which also helps them notice a fake one.

checks.narrative: A branded sign-in page tells people they are in the right place, and its absence on a phishing page is one more thing that looks wrong. It costs a few minutes and an image.

checks.title: Sign-in frequency for everyone no shorter than a working day
remediation: For each policy listed, raise the sign-in frequency to at least the threshold, or remove it and rely on the default rolling window with a persistent browser session policy.
Keep short frequencies for administrator roles and risky sign-ins, in their own policies.

userImpact.text: People are asked to sign in again less often, without losing the protection of MFA or device checks.

checks.narrative: Microsoft's guidance is that frequent reauthentication trains people to approve prompts without reading them and costs time all day. Short sign-in frequencies belong on administrator roles and risky sessions; for everyone else the default rolling window with Conditional Access does the work.

checks.title: Members can reset their own password
remediation: In Entra, Password reset, set Self service password reset enabled to All (or a group that covers every member).
Require the methods people already registered for MFA so nobody registers twice.
For hybrid identity, turn on password writeback in Entra Connect or Cloud Sync.

userImpact.text: People can reset a forgotten password from the sign-in page instead of calling the help desk.

checks.narrative: A forgotten password without self-service reset is a help desk call and an idle person. With it, the reset takes a minute, uses the MFA methods people already have, and the help desk stops verifying callers by voice, which is itself a social engineering risk.

checks.title: Sign-in name matches the email address
remediation: Decide the target: the sign-in name (UPN) should be the primary email address for every member with a mailbox.
Pilot with a few people first: their OneDrive address changes, apps and devices ask them to sign in again, and Authenticator keeps the old name until the account is re-added.
Check SaaS applications that match users by UPN in SAML before changing them, then change the UPN in Entra or, for synced users, in Active Directory.

userImpact.text: People's OneDrive address changes and every app and device asks them to sign in again; apps keyed on the old name can lose the account.

checks.narrative: Microsoft recommends the sign-in name match the email address. There is no security weakness in a mismatch; the cost is support: people try their email to sign in, Teams external chat and guest invitations address them by one name and find them by the other, and apps that match by UPN drift from those that match by email. A member signing in with an onmicrosoft.com name while mailing from the company domain is the clearest case.

checks.title: Display names read First Last
remediation: Change the display name of each person listed to First Last, in Entra or, for synced users, in Active Directory or the HR feed.
Keep the surname in the Surname attribute so the address book can still sort by it.

userImpact.text: People see their own and colleagues' names the other way round once, and the address book reads naturally afterwards.

checks.narrative: Last, First display names carry no security risk, but Microsoft 365 reads the display name as written: greetings and Copilot use the first word, so people are addressed by their surname, initials avatars come out reversed, @mentions and the people picker read surname first, and the comma breaks CSV exports and some SaaS provisioning.

checks.title: People can approve sign-ins with their phone, without a password
remediation: In Entra, Authentication methods, Microsoft Authenticator, set the authentication mode for everyone to Any (push and passwordless) rather than push only.
Tell people they can choose Use the Microsoft Authenticator app instead at sign-in and approve with the number shown, then turn on phone sign-in in the app.

userImpact.text: People who turn it on sign in by matching a number in Authenticator instead of typing a password; nothing changes for anyone who does not.

checks.narrative: Authenticator can do more than approve a second factor: with phone sign-in on, it replaces the password altogether for people who register it. Fewer passwords typed means fewer forgotten, reused and phished ones, and a faster sign-in on every new device.

checks.title: Everyone is offered their strongest sign-in method first
remediation: In Entra, Authentication methods, Settings, set System-preferred multifactor authentication to Enabled (or leave it Microsoft managed) for all users.

userImpact.text: People are prompted with their strongest registered method straight away, such as Authenticator or a passkey, instead of the last one they used or a list to pick from.

checks.narrative: Without it, sign-in offers the method a person used last, often a text message, and leaves stronger methods a click away. System-preferred MFA asks for the strongest method the person has registered, which is both safer and one decision fewer at every sign-in.

checks.title: People are nudged to set up Authenticator when they sign in
remediation: In Entra, Authentication methods, Registration campaign, set the state to Enabled (or Microsoft managed) for all users, with a short snooze limit.
Exclude only accounts that cannot use a phone, such as shared or service accounts.

userImpact.text: People still on text messages are asked once at sign-in to set up Authenticator, with a few snoozes allowed; they do it themselves instead of calling the help desk.

checks.narrative: Moving people off text messages and calls usually stalls on getting each person to install and register Authenticator. The registration campaign asks them at the moment they sign in, walks them through it, and keeps asking until it is done, so the switch happens without a help desk project.

checks.title: Windows sign-in without a password option
remediation: Once Windows Hello for Business is deployed (EP-012), create a settings catalog profile with Authentication, Enable Passwordless Experience set to Enabled, and assign it to a pilot group, then to Entra joined devices.

userImpact.text: The password option disappears from the Windows sign-in and unlock screens; people use Windows Hello (face, fingerprint or PIN), with recovery through Windows Hello or a Temporary Access Pass.

checks.narrative: With Windows Hello in place, the password is still offered on the sign-in screen, so people keep typing it and keep it alive. The passwordless experience removes it from Windows sign-in, which shortens every sign-in and leaves an attacker no password to phish or replay on that device.

checks.title: Password reset from the Windows sign-in screen, and back to AD for synced users
remediation: In a settings catalog profile for Windows, set Authentication, Allow Aad Password Reset to Allowed, so the sign-in screen shows Reset password.
For synced users, turn on password writeback in Entra Connect or Cloud Sync, so a reset in the cloud changes the AD password too.

userImpact.text: Someone locked out of their laptop can reset their password from the Windows sign-in screen with their MFA methods, and for synced users the new password works on-premises too.

checks.narrative: Self-service reset helps only if people can reach it. A person who forgot their password is usually stuck at the Windows sign-in screen, not in a browser; the reset link there turns a help desk call into two minutes. For synced accounts, writeback makes that reset count in AD as well.

checks.title: iPhones, iPads and Macs sign in once for every work app
remediation: Deploy Microsoft's Enterprise SSO plug-in: a settings catalog profile (or device features profile) with the extensible single sign-on payload for com.microsoft.azureauthenticator.ssoextension on iOS and iPadOS, and Platform SSO with com.microsoft.CompanyPortalMac.ssoextension on macOS (EP-017).
Assign it to the managed Apple devices, with Authenticator (iOS) or Company Portal (macOS) installed.

userImpact.text: People sign in once on the device and then open Outlook, Teams, Edge and other work apps without another prompt.

checks.narrative: Without the plug-in, each app on an iPhone or Mac asks for its own sign-in and its own MFA. The Enterprise SSO plug-in shares one sign-in across work apps and Safari, which removes a stream of prompts and makes device-based Conditional Access work the same way in every app.

checks.title: Update restarts give people a day's grace
remediation: In each Windows update ring, set Grace period to at least one day (two is common), so a device past its deadline does not restart the moment someone opens it.
Set active hours (or let Windows learn them) so restarts happen outside the working day.

userImpact.text: A laptop that missed its update deadline while switched off waits a day before restarting, instead of restarting minutes after it is opened.

checks.narrative: Deadlines keep devices patched, but with no grace period a device that was off over a weekend restarts as soon as it comes back, often in the middle of a meeting. A short grace period keeps the security of the deadline without the surprise restart.

checks.title: Work apps on phones unlock with Face ID or a fingerprint
remediation: In each iOS and Android app protection policy listed, under Access requirements, allow Touch ID, Face ID and fingerprint instead of the PIN (keep the PIN as the fallback).
Keep the PIN reset time and the device-level requirements as they are; biometrics replace typing, not the check.

userImpact.text: People open Outlook and Teams on their phone with Face ID or a fingerprint instead of typing a separate app PIN several times a day.

checks.narrative: An app PIN that must be typed every time Outlook or Teams opens is one of the most complained-about settings in mobile management, and people choose weak PINs to cope. Allowing the phone's biometrics keeps the protection and removes the friction.

checks.title: Licences assigned through groups
remediation: Create a group per licence package (dynamic on department or job, or fed by HR provisioning) and assign the licences to the group in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Entra.
Move people over by adding them to the group, then remove the direct assignment.

userImpact.text: Nothing changes for people already licensed; new starters get their apps on day one because their group brings the licence.

checks.narrative: Licences assigned one person at a time wait for someone to remember them: new starters sit without Teams or Outlook, leavers keep paid licences. Group-based licensing ties the licence to the group, so joining, moving and leaving take care of it.

checks.title: Profiles carry job title and department
remediation: Fill job title and department for every member, from the HR system where one exists (HR-driven provisioning, GV-011) or in Entra or AD for synced users.
Add the manager attribute at the same time, so org charts and approval routing work.

userImpact.text: People see who someone is and where they sit when they look them up in Outlook or Teams, and the org chart fills in.

checks.narrative: Profile cards in Outlook and Teams, the organisation chart, people search and dynamic groups all read job title and department. Empty fields make colleagues hard to find and leave dynamic groups and access rules with nothing to go on.

checks.title: Outlook marks mail from outside the organisation
remediation: Run Set-ExternalInOutlook -Enabled $true in Exchange Online PowerShell; add trusted partner domains with -AllowList if they should not be tagged.
Then remove any transport rule that adds [EXTERNAL] to subject lines, which breaks threading and search.

userImpact.text: Mail from outside carries an External tag in the message list and a banner in Outlook, without anything added to the subject line.

checks.narrative: People decide whether to trust a message in a second, and knowing it came from outside is the most useful hint they get. Outlook's built-in tag shows it in every client without rewriting subjects, which subject-line tags do and which break replies, threading and search.

checks.title: MailTips warn before mail goes outside or to a large audience
remediation: Run Set-OrganizationConfig -MailTipsAllTipsEnabled $true -MailTipsExternalRecipientsTipsEnabled $true, and set -MailTipsLargeAudienceThreshold to a size that fits the organisation.

userImpact.text: Outlook shows a short notice while someone writes to an outside address or a large list, before they press Send.

checks.narrative: Most data leaks by email are a wrong recipient, not an attack. A MailTip that says an external person is on the thread, or that a list goes to thousands of people, catches the mistake while it can still be fixed.

checks.title: One-click phishing report in Outlook
remediation: In Microsoft Defender, Settings, Email and collaboration, User reported settings, turn on monitoring of reported messages in Outlook with the built-in Report button, sending reports to Microsoft and to a reporting mailbox.
Tell people where the button is, and use the reports to tune filtering and training (EM-020).

userImpact.text: People get a Report button in Outlook to flag phishing in one click, and a thank-you note when they do.

checks.narrative: People who spot a phishing message often do nothing because reporting it is a chore. A Report button built into Outlook makes it a click, sends the message where the security team and Microsoft can act on it, and turns every alert user into an early warning.

checks.title: Archives grow on their own
remediation: Run Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive (or Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive per mailbox), with archive mailboxes enabled and a retention policy that moves old mail to the archive.

userImpact.text: People with large mailboxes stop getting mailbox-full warnings; older mail moves to the archive and the archive keeps growing as needed.

checks.narrative: A full mailbox stops mail arriving and sends people deleting things they may need. Auto-expanding archiving, included with Exchange Online Plan 2 and Exchange Online Archiving, adds archive space as it fills, so mailbox size stops being a problem anyone has to manage.
